title: CTS 2026 Weekly Survey 2 - Pornography and the Church
suggestion_columns: Suggest one or more future CTS survey items. Please write each suggestion as a statement that a participant could rate from 0 to 100.

source_columns: Q1
Pornography use is more spiritually damaging to churches today than most other hidden sins.
items.text: Pornography use is more spiritually damaging to churches today than most other hidden sins.

source_columns: Q2
In my ministry context, pornography use among Christian men is more common than most congregations recognize.
items.text: In my ministry context, pornography use among Christian men is more common than most congregations recognize.

source_columns: Q3
In my ministry context, pornography use among Christian women is more common than most congregations recognize.
items.text: In my ministry context, pornography use among Christian women is more common than most congregations recognize.

source_columns: Q4
Persistent pornography use should ordinarily disqualify a pastor from active ministry until repentance and accountability are demonstrably established.
items.text: Persistent pornography use should ordinarily disqualify a pastor from active ministry until repentance and accountability are demonstrably established.

source_columns: Q5
Churches should ask direct but pastorally careful questions about pornography use when evaluating candidates for leadership.
items.text: Churches should ask direct but pastorally careful questions about pornography use when evaluating candidates for leadership.

source_columns: Q6
Pornography use is substantially shaping sexual expectations within Christian marriages.
items.text: Pornography use is substantially shaping sexual expectations within Christian marriages.

source_columns: Q7
Churches should avoid presenting accountability software as a primary solution for habitual pornography use.
items.text: Churches should avoid presenting accountability software as a primary solution for habitual pornography use.

source_columns: Q8
Pastors should address pornography from the pulpit more often than most churches currently do.
items.text: Pastors should address pornography from the pulpit more often than most churches currently do.

source_columns: Q9
Churches should treat habitual pornography use as both moral sin and a behavioral health concern.
items.text: Churches should treat habitual pornography use as both moral sin and a behavioral health concern.

source_columns: In my ministry context, churches are currently losing more ground than they are gaining against pornography.
items.text: In my ministry context, churches are currently losing more ground than they are gaining against pornography.

source_columns: Churches should provide structured pastoral care for spouses harmed by pornography use even when the user is repentant.
items.text: Churches should provide structured pastoral care for spouses harmed by pornography use even when the user is repentant.

source_columns: Churches should teach young people about pornography before parents or students report that it is already a problem.
items.text: Churches should teach young people about pornography before parents or students report that it is already a problem.

source_columns: A church should require formal membership before a person serves in any public ministry role.
items.text: A church should require formal membership before a person serves in any public ministry role.

source_columns: Pastors should normally mention specific false teachers by name when their teachings are influencing the congregation.
items.text: Pastors should normally mention specific false teachers by name when their teachings are influencing the congregation.

source_columns: Christians should avoid recreational marijuana use even where it is legal.
items.text: Christians should avoid recreational marijuana use even where it is legal.
